transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, um... I guess I'm here because things just feel... off. Like, the stuff I usually enjoy doing, it just feels flat now. Heavy, I guess. I used to go on these photography walks, help out with mentoring some kids, even just... keeping my calendar organized at work. But lately, I just... I don't know. I've just stopped starting any of it. It's just too much effort.
When did you first notice that things started feeling this way? Can you remember roughly how long ago that was?

Um... I suppose it's been a while. Maybe... a year and three months? Give or take. 

It was around the time... well, a family member started having some health issues. Their behavior changed, and I had to step in and take on a lot of the coordination for them. So... yeah. It started around then.

Over this past year and three months, have there been any stretches of time — maybe a few weeks or longer — when you felt back to your normal self, or has it been pretty much constantly feeling this way?

Um... I don't know about normal. I mean, there are times when it's not the heavy feeling. 

For most of this whole time, I guess... I end up swinging back the other way. I get these stretches where I'm just... really driven. Like I don't need much sleep, and I just take on a lot of things. I feel really sure of myself then. Even if there are some quiet weeks in between, it mostly just keeps cycling back to that. So... no, not really normal.

When you describe these stretches where you feel really driven and don't need much sleep — do they start suddenly, like you can point to a day or two when things shifted? Or do they build up gradually over time?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't paid that much attention to exactly when it starts. It just... happens, I guess. I don't really keep track of the days it shifts.
During those stretches when you feel really driven and don't need much sleep — does that feeling eventually go away and then the heavy, flat feeling comes back? Or does it all just blend together?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess the driven feeling stops eventually, but... I don't know if it blends together or just switches. I just know things change. I don't really analyze it that much.
When you're in one of those stretches where you feel really driven and don't need much sleep — roughly how long do those stretches usually last before the heavy, flat feeling comes back?
I don't know... maybe a few weeks? I don't really keep a calendar of it. It just lasts for a while and then it doesn't.

When you're in those stretches feeling really driven with less need for sleep, and then it shifts back to the heavy, flat feeling — do you remember a specific point where you noticed the shift happened, or does it feel like one mood gradually blends into the other without a clear moment of change?
I don't really know. It's hard to say. I just... I don't really pay attention to a specific moment. It just changes eventually.

When you're in one of those stretches feeling really driven with less sleep, and then it switches back to feeling heavy and flat — over this past year and three months, how many separate times would you say this cycle has happened? Like, can you count roughly how many times you've gone through that shift?
I couldn't give you a number. Um... I don't keep a tally of it or anything. It just... it happens when it happens. I really haven't been counting.

When you're in those stretches where you feel really driven and don't need much sleep — besides needing less sleep, what else changes? For example, do you find yourself talking more, starting lots of new projects or plans, or does your mind feel like it's racing with ideas?

I guess people say I talk differently. My wife... and some of the people at the office, they tell me I talk really fast when I'm like that. They say I just kind of jump around from talking about medical forms to, I don't know, work deadlines, or ideas I have for mentoring the junior admins. They say they can't really get a word in. I don't really notice it myself, but... that's what they tell me.

Over this past year and three months, when you're in that heavy, flat feeling — does that feeling ever go away completely on its own, or does it always need something to happen — like the stressful situation with your family member getting better — for you to feel better?

I don't know if it goes away on its own. Um... it's just... that heavy feeling is actually why I'm here. It's just that things that usually make me feel like me, like going on photography walks or mentoring the younger staff... even just keeping my calendar organized... they all just started feeling so flat. And heavy. I just... I stopped doing them. I stopped starting things. I don't really know what makes it better or worse.

When you think back over this whole year and three months — if you were to describe it as simply as possible — would you say you've had separate, distinct periods where you felt one way, then a different period where you felt another way? Or has it mostly been one continuous mood state the whole time, just with some ups and downs mixed in?

I guess... it's mostly been separate periods. For most of this whole time, I just keep ending up back in those stretches where I'm too driven, you know? The ones where I sleep less and... take on too much. Even if I have some quieter weeks in between, it just keeps coming back to that.

Before this past year and three months, have you ever had a period — maybe weeks or months — where you felt this same heavy, flat feeling like you do now, where things felt like too much effort and you lost interest in activities you normally enjoy?
No... I don't think so. Before this last year or so, I was fine. I never really had this... heavy feeling before.

I want to make sure I understand your history correctly. Going back further — before this past year or so — have you ever had a time in your life, even just for a few weeks, where you felt this same kind of heaviness, flatness, or loss of interest in things you normally enjoyed?
I mean... like I just said, no. I really don't remember feeling this way before last year. Things were... just normal before.

I want to go back even further — in your teenage years or early adulthood, before this past year, do you remember ever having a period that lasted weeks or months where you felt depressed, sad, or just couldn't get motivated to do things?
I... no. I told you, I didn't feel like this back then. Everything was just... fine. I didn't have these problems when I was younger.
